result: 26 target-bounded sites remain across 16 functions. Six groups closed (SLH 6, hw 25, legacy 2, decoder 3, export-callback 4 reachable, capabilities 4) reducing element 7 from 67 to 26. buckets.bucket: export-callback blocked on the header/parameter question
buckets.why_open: These were among the thirteen claimed by the rejected chain batch. That batch's own mutation showed eight of them depended on an undisclosed header-gate rewrite (_strip_preprocessor), not on chain provenance. The chain-only re-land correctly closed the four that do depend on chain steps and left these.
buckets.evidence_needed: a legitimate resolution of why the header/parameter check does not accept them: either the check is wrong (fix it, with a fixture per case) or the operand genuinely is not an exported parameter (keep refusing). This must not be solved by rewriting the header gate without disclosure again.
buckets.risk: medium — the previous attempt to close these was rejected for exactly this

buckets.why_open: an exported registration API, a DSO or a provider fills a stored slot. A static target set is incomplete by construction (the application can register), and parameter forwarding cannot see a store.
buckets.evidence_needed: a store-witness instrument: for each slot, prove the set of writers reachable from the consumer, or bind the slot to a declared registration ABI with the registration entry point checked. This is a new mechanism and needs BOUNDARY review, mutation controls and a negative control where a registered slot is genuinely open.
buckets.risk: high — the target set is open by design, so any acceptance must be an ABI-contract argument, not a finite enumeration

buckets.why_open: compiler-merged: one indirect call serves two slots because the branches converge, so the operand has two reaching definitions and the provenance rule refuses multi-definition origins.
buckets.evidence_needed: the merged-site witness already drafted (every reaching definition independently justified, all offsets table-declared, union of slot ids recorded) with its three controls and a BOUNDARY review.
buckets.risk: low-medium — the shape is understood; the risk is in the phi-equivalent rule

buckets.why_open: the value is push $0x0 or lea of an in-image function through a stack argument; it is a constant, not an exported entry parameter. The pk8 case is additionally blocked by the argument model not handling push (E7CB-R1).
buckets.evidence_needed: none for the two pkcs12 paths: they should stay refused permanently and be recorded as such. The pk8 path becomes attributable only if the push model is fixed, and even then it must satisfy the entry-parameter requirement.
buckets.risk: none (two permanent) / low (pk8, contingent on E7CB-R1)
